end.summary:
Practised distinguishing point, line segment, line and ray by endpoints and arrows.
Aryan correctly described a segment as having two endpoints and fixed length.
Aryan correctly described a line as extending infinitely in both directions with no endpoints.
Aryan initially treated a ray as having two endpoints; later corrected this to one endpoint and one direction.
Applied the ideas to identify segment, ray and line diagrams.
end.parentNote: Aryan practised identifying geometric figures using endpoints, arrows, direction, and length. They used the ruler example for a segment and the torch-beam example to discuss a ray. Aryan first said a ray has two endpoints, but later corrected this and explained that it starts at one point and continues in one direction. At home, ask them to draw one segment, one ray, and one line, then label their endpoints and arrows.
